USMLE-style practice · Pediatrics

Discharge after sustained improvement

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A child treated for croup has completed the recommended post-epinephrine observation period. He is alert, drinking, breathing comfortably and has no stridor at rest. Which additional discharge element is most important for safe home management?

  1. Clear return precautions and reliable access to reassessment
  2. Routine antibiotics to prevent bacterial superinfection
  3. Scheduled home epinephrine without observation arrangements
  4. Follow-up only after all cough has resolved
  5. Nightly sedating cough medication to prevent agitation
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Clear return precautions and reliable access to reassessment

Caregivers should recognize recurrent rest stridor, increased effort, poor intake or altered alertness and know how to obtain help.

Understanding the options

Clear return precautions and reliable access to reassessment
Caregivers should recognize recurrent rest stridor, increased effort, poor intake or altered alertness and know how to obtain help.
Routine antibiotics to prevent bacterial superinfection
Prophylactic antibiotics are not standard after uncomplicated croup recovery.
Scheduled home epinephrine without observation arrangements
Epinephrine is short acting and requires appropriate monitoring; this is not a substitute for a safe discharge plan.
Follow-up only after all cough has resolved
Caregivers need to seek help promptly for deterioration, even while some expected cough remains.
Nightly sedating cough medication to prevent agitation
Sedating cough remedies do not treat croup and can compromise recognition or management of deterioration.
